content: Norethindrone's metabolism may be influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 activity. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. Indinavir can elevate the levels or effects of norgestrel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor accordingly. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially raising the risk of adverse effects. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. If co-administration is necessary, oliceridine dosing may need to be less frequent. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses as needed. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Indinavir raises the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Similarly, indinavir increases ondansetron levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. While CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance, no dosage adjustment is recommended. Orlistat reduces indinavir levels or effects by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concurrently. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if an increased viral load is confirmed. Indinavir elevates osilodrostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Indinavir also increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Oxcarbazepine decreases indinavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir increases paclitaxel levels or effects through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Similarly, indinavir raises levels of paliperidone, panobinostat, paricalcitol, and paromomycin via CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised for panobinostat, with a reduced starting dose of 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital reduce indinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor. Phenytoin similarly decreases indinavir levels through these mechanisms. Indinavir increases pitavastatin toxicity due to OATP1B1 inhibition, raising the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE-related metabolites, with MMAE being a CYP3A4 substrate. Use caution and monitor. Ponatinib increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Posaconazole raises indinavir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir reduces pramlintide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir increases pravastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition, raising myopathy risk. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates praziquantel, prednisolone, and prednisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Primidone decreases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Quercetin reduces indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir increases quetiapine and quinidine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Quinupristin/dalfopristin raises indinavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ranolazine increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates repaglinide levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ribociclib increases indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Indinavir raises rifabutin levels by reducing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rifampin and rifapentine decrease indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir increases rilpivirine and riociguat levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates ripretinib levels, including its active metabolite DP-5439, by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir raises risperidone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir and ritonavir mutually increase each other's levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein inhibition, raising the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir reduces rosiglitazone effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. Rucaparib raises indinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Rufinamide decreases indinavir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates sacubitril/valsartan levels, with valsartan being a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Use caution and monitor. Sarecycline increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and consider dosage reductions for P-gp substrates when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Indinavir raises saxagliptin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Indinavir increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Indinavir elevates sertraline levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir raises sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicities if used concomitantly. Patients on indinavir with ritonavir should not exceed 25 mg of sildenafil for erectile dysfunction within a 48-hour period. For other protease inhibitors, a lower initial sildenafil dose of 25 mg is recommended. Indinavir increases silodosin and sirolimus levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir reduces sitagliptin effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH, applicable only to oral forms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Indinavir elevates sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, solifenacin, and sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. St. John’s Wort reduces indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Stiripentol increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Indinavir raises streptomycin and sufentanil SL levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. Indinavir elevates sunitinib, tacrolimus, tasimelteon, and temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Tacrolimus ointment levels are also increased by indinavir.
